title: Article 231 — Establishment of a common High Court for two or more States

content.overview: Article 231 provides that Parliament may by law establish a common High Court for two or more States or for two or more States and a Union territory. Provisions of Chapter V of Part VI apply subject to modifications specified in the article (including adaptation of references to Governor and State).
content.glance: Parliament may by law establish a common High Court for two or more States, or States and a UT.
content.study:
Article 231 enables a common High Court:
- For two or more States; or
- For two or more States and a Union territory.

Parliamentary law establishes such a Court; Chapter V applies with modifications (e.g. references to the Governor adapted as provided).

Examination: parliamentary law; two or more States; States + UT; modifications to Chapter V.

sections.heading: Key rule
sections.body: Parliament may by law establish a common High Court for two or more States or for two or more States and a Union territory. Chapter V applies with the modifications set out in the article.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Can there be a common High Court for more than one State?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Yes. Under Article 231, Parliament may by law establish a common High Court for two or more States or for two or more States and a Union territory. The provisions of Chapter V of Part VI apply in relation to such a High Court subject to the modifications specified in the article.

keyTakeaways: Art 231: common High Court for two or more States / States+UT.
